title: Benchmark launches gallium and germanium metal price assessments
gist: Benchmark launched biweekly gallium and germanium metal price assessments (CIF Europe) to add transparency to small, China-dominated byproduct markets (about 86% of refined gallium, two thirds of refined germanium) under tightening Chinese export licensing.

insights.claim: China accounts for around 86% of refined gallium production and roughly two thirds of refined germanium.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Extreme concentration makes both metals a lever in trade disputes; monitor ex-China refining announcements.
insights.quote: China accounts for around 86% of refined gallium production and roughly two thirds of refined germanium
insights.locator: According to Benchmark's Gallium and Germanium Services

insights.claim: Beijing introduced export licensing on gallium and germanium in August 2023 and has since tightened controls, leaving buyers outside China with restricted availability, volatile pricing and few reliable reference points.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Export licensing creates a price gap and volatility outside China, which benefits non-Chinese suppliers and stockholders.

insights.claim: Ex-China refining capacity for gallium and germanium is building slowly because both are byproducts that can only be recovered where a host operation has the equipment and a commercial reason to extract them.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Supply response is structurally slow; byproduct economics, not just capital, gate new supply, so shortages may persist.
insights.locator: A limited number of refiners outside of China

insights.claim: Gallium and germanium are recovered as byproducts of aluminium and zinc processing.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Supply is tied to aluminium and zinc operations, so host-metal producers hold optionality.

insights.claim: Gallium is used in compound semiconductors underpinning power electronics, 5G networks, LEDs and radar.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Gallium disruption would hit power electronics and telecom supply chains.
insights.locator: Gallium is used in compound semiconductors

insights.claim: Germanium is used in fibre optic cables, infrared optics, thermal imaging and satellite solar cells, and both metals have defence applications.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Defence and space demand makes these metals priority targets for government stockpiling and supply-chain funding.
insights.locator: Germanium is used in fibre optic cables

insights.claim: Benchmark will publish gallium (99.99%) and germanium (99.999%) metal prices, CIF Europe in USD per tonne, every other Thursday, based on transacted prices from engagement with market participants.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A published reference price enables index-linked contracts and hedging in previously opaque markets.

insights.claim: Benchmark argues gallium and germanium are small markets with an outsized strategic role, and that buyers outside China have had very little price information.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Price discovery is a precondition for ex-China investment; note this is also vendor marketing for Benchmark's services.
insights.quote: Gallium and germanium are small markets with an outsized strategic role, and with China restricting exports, buyers outside China have had very little price information to work from
